name: HM7B
tagline: Ariane's cryogenic upper stage, three decades of service
description: The HM7B is the hydrogen-fuelled upper-stage engine that gave Ariane rockets a high-energy kick after the core stage shut down. Running a gas-generator cycle on LOX and LH2, it first flew on Ariane 2 in May 1986 and continued through the end of Ariane 5's operational life in July 2023. Its small size belies a high specific impulse that made it the workhorse for geostationary transfer injections, carrying commercial satellites and scientific payloads — including Rosetta, Mars Express, and Venus Express — to their departure trajectories over more than three decades.
best_known_for: Europe's cryogenic upper-stage engine — Ariane's translunar workhorse
